[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
Thomas was born on 1 May 1777 and baptised on 7 May in Rathdowney Catholic parish, Queen’s County (now Laois), Ireland, the son of [[Glasgow-3593|David Glascow]] and [[Ford-28175|Anne Ford]].<ref name="Rathdowney1777">Rathdowney Catholic parish register, NLI microfilm 05013/08, image 83, manuscript p.147, Thomas entry near the foot of the right-hand page; [https://registers.nli.ie/pages/vtls000631901_083 National Library of Ireland original scan], inspected 22 October 2026. Born 1 May; baptised 7 May 1777; parents David Glascow and Anne Ford. Household place and sponsors remain unread.</ref><ref>"Ireland, Catholic Parish Registers, 1740-1900", FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:X3QK-WMQL : Fri Mar 28 00:01:13 UTC 2025), Entry for Thoms Glascow and David Glascow, 7 May 1777.
</ref>
His parents [[Glasgow-3593|David Glascow]] and [[Ford-28175|Anne Ford]] married at Rathdowney on 14 September 1773.<ref>[https://registers.nli.ie/registers/vtls000631901#page/150/mode/1up Rathdowney Catholic parish register, NLI microfilm 05013/08, image 150, right-hand page, marriage entry dated 14 September 1773].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Rathdowney baptism, reviewed 22 October 2026 ===

This assessment identifies the register child represented by [[Glasgow-3592]] and his expressly named parents. It does not prove that this child became the Tipperary husband of [[Ryan-23770|Johanna Ryan]] or father of [[Glasgow-3595|Michael Glasgow]], and does not identify David with the Scottish [[Glasgow-3456|David Glasgow]]. [[Glasgow-3594|Margaret]]’s separate baptism and the 1773 marriage have not been inspected in this batch. The household townland and sponsors are not securely read from the available low-resolution scan and are not asserted here.

At that review, the next proposed test was to read the 14 September 1773 marriage and Margaret’s July 1774 entry for the household place and witnesses, then test the later Thomas–Johanna–Michael identification against original Tipperary records. David’s own parents remain unknown; his before-1755 birth is an adult-marriage estimate, not a record of his birthplace or age.


=== Possible Thomas Glasgow, Kentucky postal addressee, 1799 ===
Thomas Glasgow, Kentucky, is named in a list of letters remaining at the Lexington post office, printed 24 January 1799.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/1181678638/ Kentucky Gazette, 1799-01-24, p.3].</ref>

Kentucky is the printed qualifier. The postal list gives no age, occupation, family or evidence of continuous residence.

This may concern [[Glasgow-3592]]. Recorded exact 1 May 1777 Rathdowney birth permits age 21 in 1799; Irish birthplace and inherited family provide no Kentucky or postal identification.

=== Original Rathdowney marriage — 24 October 2026 ===

The witness line appears to read ‘Michl Grady & Marg Conor’; both abbreviated forenames and the Conor surname reading remain tentative. The register supplies no age or named parents, and its marginal Rathdowney/C. Do notation does not establish an exact townland. The marriage is consistent with the couple named in Thomas’s 1777 baptism; existing parent assessments remain 98%, and no later adult identity is resolved.
